title: What's with the Winchester Mystery House?
summary: Josh and Chuck run a Halloween-edition episode on the Winchester Mystery House in San Jose, California. They cover Sarah Winchester's background as heir to the Winchester Repeating Arms fortune, the death of her infant daughter Annie and husband William, her visit to a Boston medium (Adam Coots) who told her the spirits of people killed by Winchester rifles required a never-ending house, and her move west to build the house nonstop with foreman John Hanson. They describe the seance routine, the odd design features (stairs to nowhere, doors opening onto drops, two mirrors), her innovations, the 1906 earthquake that led her to seal off rooms, her death, the auction of the contents, and the house as a tourist attraction. A listener mail segment about a proposed coordinate-plane model of sexuality (from Paul of Uniontown, PA) closes the episode.

segments.title: Halloween opening and candy corn
segments.summary: Hosts open the Halloween edition with candy corn banter and introduce the Winchester Mystery House as their topic.

segments.title: Overview of the Winchester house and Sarah's background
segments.summary: The house is described as a huge Victorian mansion of uncertain room count on former rural land near San Jose. Sarah Winchester, born in 1839, married William Winchester, heir to the Winchester Repeating Arms fortune, and the repeating rifle is discussed.

segments.title: Death of daughter and husband
segments.summary: Sarah's infant daughter Annie died of marasmus in infancy, and William Winchester later died at age forty three. The hosts discuss infant mortality and life expectancy, including a listener correction about it.

segments.title: Boston medium and the curse
segments.summary: Sarah visits Boston medium Adam Coots, who tells her the spirits of people killed by Winchester rifles haunt the family and that she must build a house without end. She moves west to California and buys land three miles west of San Jose.

segments.title: Seances, construction routine and pay
segments.summary: Sarah acts as her own architect, takes instructions from seances in the Blue Room, and runs round-the-clock construction with foreman John Hanson, paying double the day rate. Her charity and seclusion are described.

segments.title: Odd design features and innovations
segments.summary: The hosts describe the strange architecture, including switchback stairs, stairs to nowhere, doors opening onto drops, and hidden corridors. They also cover her real innovations such as wool insulation, carbide gas lighting, electric push buttons and the annunciator servant call system.

segments.title: 1906 earthquake, later years, death and auction
segments.summary: The 1906 earthquake frightens Sarah, who seals off damaged sections and moves to a houseboat for six years. After her death, construction stopped and the contents were auctioned over six weeks. The house became a tourist attraction, and a documentary, Mrs Winchester's House, narrated by Lilian Gish, is recommended.

segments.title: Listener mail on sexuality coordinate plane
segments.summary: A listener from Uniontown, PA, Paul, suggests plotting sexual orientation and sexual intensity on a coordinate plane. The hosts discuss and praise the idea.
